name: Sable Freight Thermal Henley
description:
A long-sleeve thermal henley from Sable Freight, a workwear brand that started supplying cold-chain logistics workers and has since expanded into general industrial apparel. The fabric is a waffle-knit thermal cotton-poly in off-white, heather grey, or dark brown, with a three-button placket at the neck and flat-locked seams throughout to reduce pressure points under heavier outerwear. The cuffs are slightly extended to stay tucked into gloves.

This is a base layer that gets worn as an outer layer because it looks like one. The cut is relaxed enough to be comfortable over a full shift and fitted enough not to bunch under a jacket. Sable Freight henleys show up in fabrication plants, on delivery crews, and in the kitchens of Tier 2 restaurants. They also show up on Tier 3 people who want something that looks like it works for a living.
what_it_says: You're practical, you run cold, and you've probably had this shirt for at least two years.
worn_by: Tier 3 people who like the aesthetic
story_hooks: Sable Freight's main client is a cold-storage corponation that uses the brand's uniform program to track worker movement — the henleys have no tech, but the belt clips distributed alongside them do.
A Tier 3 designer has been photographed repeatedly in a Sable Freight henley, and now the brand is getting orders it doesn't know how to handle from a demographic it never targeted.
A character wearing a Sable Freight henley is mistaken for a maintenance worker in a restricted facility — and decides to play along.
